utterances.text: I first want to discuss a little bit about your appointment to becoming the chief of the -- very well. Let me rephrase. Let me rephrase. Before being appointed to your position, as I understand it, you were just a soldier. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there was an incident where a couple of prisoners had escaped and all of a sudden there was a change of personnel, and that's how you inherited your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And along with you, there was a gentleman by the name of Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was a deputy, was he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it when you were being questioned by the Prosecution in Banja Luka back in November 28th, 2001, you described Mr. Petrovic as a good man, an honest man, and conscientious and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall seeing that in fact in the transcript of your statement that was made of your -- the statement that you gave in Banja Luka? That's in there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anything from Banja Luka. Everything I stated there was tape recorded. It was said to me that the Prosecution would send me those tapes. I never received those tapes, but that doesn't matter. I am trying to speak about everything to the best of my recollection. Whatever I succeed in recollecting, I will tell you in the best interest of justice. My aim is to assist you, to assist the Prosecution, to assist the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just so we are precise, I would like to show you your statement, a copy of your statement, and I will point you in the right direction and see if it accurately reflects what you have indicated. And I'm referring to now what has been marked as D-68/1. And if you could turn in your version to page 11 and look for lines 8 to 12 -- 8 to 10 while the rest of us in the English version will turn to page 10, lines 3 to 5. Page 11, lines 8 to 10 in your version. Okay. Now, in line 1 in the English version it states that: "Next to you that there was a deputy, Mile Petrovic." And then further down on line 3 you say: "He was appointed to the post by the command because he was a good man, honest, and conscientious and so on." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you said that of Mr. Petrovic, did you believe it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you still believe it today, that he is a good man, an honest man, and a conscientious man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, I understand yesterday you indicated that you had gone to the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Recently I was summoned, I'm not sure what the date was, and I gave a statement at the police station to inspectors of the criminal department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that was in regards to an incident that had gotten some publicity in the paper with respect to your deputy -- with respect to Mr. Petrovic being accused by Mr. Nikolic of killing six -- five to six Muslim prisoners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The summons said that I should report to the police headquarters in connection with events in Srebrenica in July 1995. That's roughly what it said. I was not the only one summoned. As far as I knew, they were summoning many people. Practically all members of the Bratunac Brigade were being summoned by the Ministry of the Interior, because they were gathering information related to events the July 1995 in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. During that occasion, were you questioned at all about the time when you were in the APC with Mr. Petrovic and Mr. Nikolic where you went down towards Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I would like to go over what Mr. Nikolic has indicated in this courtroom with respect to that particular trip. And then having laid that foundation, I will then ask you a series of questions. All right. And now I'm referring to the transcript on page 1719, line 25, and I will be reading for the next couple pages. It says: "After that, I, you, and Mile Petrovic, that is," and he describes your position. "The deputy police commander from the compound of the Bratunac Brigade barracks, we took an APC," which you knew how to drive, "and we drove off to the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road." Further down on page 1720 it says, and I'm reading from line 23: "As we moved along in this APC, you," and I'm not reading your name just for the record, you were driving. Mile Petrovic used a loudspeaker which was in the APC, and I sat on the APC. We drove from Kravica towards Konjevic Polje, and after Sandici, Mile Petrovic took the megaphone and called on the Muslims to surrender, the Muslims who were in the woods along the road." Let me stop here, and I've read all the way to page 1721, line 2. Now, sir, as I understand your testimony yesterday, you did not indicate that Mr. Petrovic was using a loudspeaker, calling on the Muslims to surrender. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. He did not use a megaphone. I already said how the megaphone was used and who used the megaphone. We did not have a megaphone and Mile did not use one at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And of course when you were questioned by the Prosecution, you didn't tell them that Mile Petrovic was using a megaphone either? In other words, what you told the Prosecutor in Banja Luka is the same thing of what you said here today?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We never got that story.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour. I'll rephrase. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- so if Mr. Nikolic stated that here in this courtroom under oath, that would have been false? I can't say that he lied, so we'll use the more -- the softer version. This would be false, that Mile Petrovic used the loudspeaker while you were driving the APC?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I say something? I'm not justifying this, but I can understand -- I mean, I know how much I can remember after all this time, how much I can remember certain things. And I can understand that Nikolic may have not remembered all these things. But I remember this. I remember this exactly, that we did not have a megaphone. And I already said that the vehicle was white and blue and it had that rotating light and then there's that loudspeaker between the rotating lights, and I know that that vehicle was used in front of us, about 200 to 300 metres in front of us. I did not even understand what they were saying, because you know the echo that is there, and of course the APC is very loud, too. And then there is this valley and the reverberations of the voice, so you cannot really understand what is being said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So I take it that you believe that perhaps Mr. Nikolic might be confused on this one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably. I don't know for what reason he would make such a statement if it were not true, especially under oath. I mean, if he stated that intentionally, then he is harming himself. He is committing perjury, because of course he took an oath like I did and like everyone else did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. You then indicate -- he then indicates on page 1721, and I'm reading from line 8: "When we stopped on that occasion, five or six Muslim soldiers surrendered to us. We took them into the APC and continued on our way to Konjevic Polje." Five or six Muslim soldiers, that's the number that he has given. My question: Yesterday you indicated that it was your recollection that it was only two. Do you still hold to that number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is certain that there were two of them. With 100 per cent certainty, there were two of them. If there were five or six of them, I guess I would have to remember that there were more of them, so there were two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So can we say that on this one, as far as you are concerned, Mr. Nikolic is wrong? We won't say whether he's fabricating it or whether he's confused, we'll use a neutral term and say he's wrong.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably. I've already said in relation to his previous statement that Mile Petrovic -- I mean, that Mile Petrovic had a megaphone. I don't know. He probably got confused on that one. And then this number, five to six, I don't know how he could have stated something like that. I mean ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move along and see what else does he state. And I'm going to read from line 12, same page, 1721. He says: "We reached Konjevic Polje. I got off the armoured personnel carrier and told Mile Petrovic to take the prisoners to a group of other prisoners who were already there. And I went and I sat down under the eaves of a house that had been burnt and where a certain number of Muslims were sitting there already, captured Muslims. I told him, that is Petrovic, I told him to take those Muslims to join that group and after that to come back to the spot where I was." Then he's asked a question by Mr. McCloskey over here. "And what happened then?" This is what Mr. Nikolic said under oath in this courtroom: "After some ten minutes or so, I heard a burst of fire not far from the spot where I was. And then -- and this burst of fire reached me from the direction of the building where the petrol station is now. This was on the bank of the River Jadar. Shortly after that burst of that fire, Mile Petrovic came under this awning where I was sitting and told me the following." And I quote, this is Nikolic quoting what Petrovic told him, page 1721, line 24 to 25. He says: "Chief, I've taken revenge for my brother and I've killed them." Now, did you see -- sir, this is a question to you. Did you see Mr. Petrovic taking five or six Muslims behind the building and returning ten minutes later? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're certain about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- and then further down the line on page 1722 he's asked the question -- Mr. McCloskey here asks Nikolic who was sitting right there where you are sitting facing all of us. "So what did you guys do after that?" That was line 8. The answer: "After that, together with you and Mile Petrovic, I returned to the Bratunac Brigade." Now, as I understand your testimony, first of all you were not aware of Mr. Petrovic taking anyone behind a building. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're not aware of Mr. Petrovic killing anyone on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it or did I hear him say something that he said to Mr. Nikolic, I killed someone or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever say to you that he had to take revenge because of his brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. He never said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And on this one here -- this occasion, this description by Mr. Nikolic, would you not say that he is wrong on this one as well, based on what you saw when you were there at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said already that this was wrong about the megaphone. Also, that it was wrong, the number of persons who got out of the woods and went to Konjevic Polje. And secondly -- or rather, thirdly, that these persons, as he said five or six persons, that Petrovic took them somewhere behind a building, that he came, then gunfire was heard all over, you see. Gunfire was heard from the road, the soldiers that were lined up along the road facing the woods, and that is where Muslims were coming out of, towards the road. They would call out to them without any kind of loudspeaker or anything, just speaking. Then when no one would show up, then they would take rifles and shoot at random at the woods, because it was a thicket, the woods were thick, and gunfire could be heard. Now, I don't know. I mean, I'm saying that I did not see Petrovic take five or six people. Those two were handed over and they were taken to where the others where. I didn't hear him say anything either. So by this very statement of mine, I claim that this was a matter of misspeaking or not remembering right or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about that. Here we have Nikolic accusing the deputy commander of the Bratunac military police of executing five or six people. All right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what it turns out to be, that he accused this Petrovic of having done that. But I'm saying that I don't know anything about this and that as a matter of fact there weren't two -- there weren't five or six men there, there were two. I did not hear this statement that he said that he was supposed to take revenge because of his brother or anything like that. I didn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you knew that Mr. Petrovic had lost a brother. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I knew that. I think that -- I think -- I may finish?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that during this attack on the village that Petrovic came from, the village of Bjelovac, that on that occasion -- I think, I'm not sure. I think he was wounded too. Now I don't know whether this is correct or not, but I think that civilians and military people who were there then -- I mean, they were killed and everything was burned --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That information was not a secret. Someone like Momir Nikolic would have known that piece of fact if he wanted to inject it into his story that Petrovic was involved in killing five or six individuals.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I know that everybody knew -- it's a small town and everybody knows who was killed and how many people were killed, women, children, military-aged men, civilians, soldiers, all of that was known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now that I've read to you Mr. Nikolic's statement, do you still think that Mr. Petrovic is a good man, an honest man, and conscientious and so on. Do you still believe that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all means. I still think so. That is my assessment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you came to The Hague, you stopped at the Prosecution's office where they prepared you to come here and testify. Do you remember that? It might have been Sunday, it might have been Saturday. It might have been both days. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on Sunday. I spoke to the Prosecution. As a matter of fact I even came to the courtroom here. They showed me where the Court would be sitting, where the Defence would be, where I would be. They showed me all of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that was just to get you familiarised with what was going to happen, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from your conversations with the Prosecution, they prepared some notes based on what you had told them and sort of questions that they had asked you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have a chance to look at those notes? Were they ever provided to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we won't go into the notes just yet, but -- why don't we, since we have them here and they're handy. Let me show you now what has been marked for identification purposes as D-69/1. And if you could just look at the top -- at the first page, the heading of it, it should read: "Proofing notes in relation," and it has your name. Do you see that, just the first line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to make sure that I'm showing you the right piece of paper. That's all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you could go to the very last page, the last page, flip it over. And at the last paragraph it says here that you were shown Defence Exhibit D-37 and D-38 and in parenthesis it says statements of Mile Petrovic and that you were asked to comment on them. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. May I ask -- may I ask you a question? Go ahead and read the whole paragraph since you're at it. Now, when these exhibits were shown to you, the statements, did you get a good chance, a good opportunity, to read them carefully?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part -- for the most part, I saw what was essential.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His recollections approximately coincide with my own, so I know -- I mean, the Prosecution told me that Petrovic gave a statement in his village, in the village of Bjelovac, and he gave a statement either to the Defence or the Prosecution, I don't know who he gave this statement to, so they showed it to me. And as for the MUP, I gave my statement on the same day. He was there before me and then I came after him. I did not even know that he had been there before that making a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understand it -- now, when you were back in Bratunac at MUP at the police station, you ran into Mr. Petrovic, and that's where he informed you that he had been hearing or he had read some article about accusations made towards him by Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not see him then. He was there before giving his statement and then he had finished giving a statement. And then when I entered the police building, his wife shot by me. And she said, "Where's my husband?" And she ran upstairs. The duty policeman was shouting, "Madam, stop. Where are you going? Who is your husband?" And she was just shouting, "Where's my husband? Where's my husband?" and she ran upstairs. And I knew that this was Petrovic's wife. And she went upstairs. She opened the door of the room where I had been asked to come. And when she opened this door, panic stricken and asked, "Where is my husband?" the inspector asked her, "Who is your husband, madam?" And she said "Mile Petrovic." And the inspector then said, "Your husband left. He said that you were waiting for him by the medical centre." She was all pale and frightened and she passed by me as she went over there. They had lost each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But in the last sentence of your proofing notes it says that at some point when you spoke to Mr. Petrovic about the accusations, he advised you that you should just tell the truth. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said to him, "Say the truth and never be afraid. If the Court considers you guilty of anything, the truth will always prevail. The truth can be concealed perhaps for a while, but the truth always surfaces. So stand by the truth and don't be afraid of anything." And he said that perhaps this newspaper -- I don't know, we said we were vilified or something like that and I said, "I'm not afraid of anything. Let anyone write whatever they want to." I mean, journalists can write all sorts of things. Journalists are journalists. Perhaps Nikolic didn't even state that. How can I know what they write and how they can word a statement. It wasn't an official document. It's not that I heard officially that Nikolic had stated that. It was in -- it was an excerpt from a newspaper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I would like right now to go over Mr. Petrovic's statement that he gave at the police station with you, and I'm going to go step by step and to see whether his statement coincides with your memory of the events as they occurred back then. So let me show you what has been marked for identification purposes as D-37/1. D-37/1 -- I'm sorry. Wrong number. It should be D-38. I apologise. We'll get to D-37 after we get to D-38. D-38/1?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The witness has said he thought there was the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm entitled to do my cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can stipulate and help out in any way, I will. I don't see why we need to go all through the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If the Prosecution wants to concede that Mr. Nikolic lied under oath, I will forego this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no. That's not a subject matter for us to discuss. I think the Judges will make our decisions at a later stage. But, Mr. Karnavas, do not repeat whatever we have already gone through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am not repeating, however I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think your point is very clear. If you have some new issues that you will bring out, you could do it, but do not repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I want to say that I want to establish a fine record, and the gentleman has indicated what he believes. We went through Nikolic's statement under oath. I now want to go through these two different statements and again ask him the questions, because I want to nail down this point. Because the Prosecution is going to argue who's to say -- because this gentleman wasn't next to Petrovic, who's to say that there wasn't an opportunity for him to take five or six people behind a building and kill them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, but just bear in mind my warnings to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. I will try to be efficient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look now at what has been marked as D-38/1. If you could just look at the top of the page and then look through it and tell me if this document looks familiar. Was this a document showed to you by the Prosecutor on Sunday when they were briefing you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know now whether it's this document. I think I saw this document, too, but there's this statement which was taken in Bjelovac, because I saw that it said, "Statement taken in the village of Bjelovac." It means that there's another document too and I think I saw that because I got this document too or rather a similar one. When I made a statement, they gave me a copy at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, we're going to get to the other statement. My questions are very precise. Was this is document that was shown to you by the Prosecutor on Sunday? Do you recall seeing this document? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it says here that it was on the first line that it was compiled on 25 August, 2003. Would that be about the time that you recollect when you went to the police department to give a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have my statement here with me in The Hague. It's at my hotel room. It's the same date, I think. Because we were there on the same day, so I think it's the same date. The Prosecution or the Defence, if they already have Petrovic's statement, they should have my statement, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree. I totally agree. I've been trying to get it. Now, I understand you told the Prosecution that you gave a statement. Did they bother to ask you to provide them with a copy of your statement so that the rest of us could have it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Mr. Karnavas, it's not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think it's very highly relevant, Your Honour, because we are trying to get to the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's have our break now and think it over during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I could just take a moment to introduce the Trial Chamber to a member of the team who will be helping us out in court. This is Salvador Viada from Spain. And you will be seeing a little more of Salvador in the coming days. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Welcome on board. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We always welcome more OTP members on the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let us get back to what has been marked as D-38/1. That was the statement that was given to you, the one that was provided by Mr. Petrovic to the Bratunac police back on 25 August 2003. If you go to the second page, you'll see where there's one part in that page where it has a heading called "statement." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In the first part of the statement, probably three or four lines down, it states -- I'll just read it. See if you can follow along. "In July as well as the previous couple of months, I was frequently absent from my unit, that is the military police platoon, because my newly born child was in poor health, so I had to devote more attention to it. That is why during those months I would often be absent for two or three hours at a stretch and I also would be given a day or two off." Then it goes on: "I point this out because due to my frequent absences, I was insufficiently aware of the events in my own unit. My commander," and he mentions your name, "was" aware of my absences." Now, let's stop there. Do you recall whether or not Mr. Petrovic had a newly born child and as a result of its sickness, Mr. Petrovic had to go home occasionally to attend to family matters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware that he had a child and that there was some problems related to the child, some health problems. Now, how often he was absent, I really don't know or on what specific days, but I know that he did have problems with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So this part of the statement would be true based on your memory of the events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, further down he says that sometime in July, he says: "I don't know the date, but I know it was early in July when on my way to the Bratunac command, that is, a military police station, I met Momir Nikolic who ordered me to wait for him at the police station. When I arrived at the station, I asked the duty officer where the commander was so that I could report to him. He told me that he was behind the station building in the," looks like, parking lot, "trying to start the engine of an armoured personnel carrier. I went behind the building and told the commander that Nikolic had ordered the two of us to wait for him." Then it goes down -- well, do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember these details, not the details, but I do know that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Further on it says: "When Nikolic came, he ordered," and he mentions you, "to start the engine of the armoured personnel carrier, which he did." That is that you did. "He told me to get in the armoured personnel carrier. Momir Nikolic got into the armoured personnel carrier and told you to drive to Konjevic Polje." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then further down, next point: "While you drove, Momir and I were inside the armoured personnel carrier. Both of us were standing, that is, I was standing at the mounted anti-aircraft machine gun and Momir was beside me at the command post." Do you recall -- is that how it was based on your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, you are not going to read all the text?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No. I just have some points. I just want to verify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Try to, you know, focus on the major points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am -- well, okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have no objection to paraphrasing the major points. Reading is not really appropriate in this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's nothing inappropriate about it, but I don't want to draw an objection that I'm mischaracterising. And I'm trying to be efficient, so I'll try the middle way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Further down it says that he noticed that on the left side of the road there were two men in civilian clothes and that Nikolic told you to stop the APC. Now is that a correct fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nikolic pulled me. I couldn't hear him because of the noise that the APC was making. He pulled me by the collar and told me to pull over. Because I didn't myself notice the people who coming down onto the road, but he was behind my back and he pulled me by the collar. So I stopped the vehicle and then I realised why I had to stop because two people were headed our way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then Mr. Petrovic says that all of you went to Konjevic Polje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I can't quite remember whether returning from Konjevic Polje to Bratunac or if it was after we had got to Konjevic Polje already. I can't remember whether it was just after we left for Konjevic Polje that we picked up these two persons or sort of going back. That's one thing I can't remember. It's a bit unclear the way I remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then Mr. Petrovic says that you and he remained in the APC while Momir took the two men to a nearby house. Do you recall that? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall who took them. There were soldiers there. I don't know who took them. There were some soldiers there and I don't think it was either Petrovic or Nikolic that took them, but rather they were probably taken as far as the midpoint of the junction and then they were taken over by other soldiers who were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop and ask you, at that point did you ever see Mr. Petrovic taking those prisoners or other prisoners to take them around a house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it had that occurred, had that occurred, given from where you were, you would have been able to see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So nothing was covering your face? You were able to see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a large junction there with buildings there, too, but yes, you could see everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also where I was with my APC you could see everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then he states that, further down in the statement, and I'll paraphrase, that that's when you met a couple of foreigners. And Momir Nikolic began speaking to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated things just the way they were. I said that two members of the Dutch Battalion came along. They came along and as soon as they arrived, my impression was that they had arrived from the woods, but I wasn't sure because I didn't speak their language. There was no way for us to communicate. They tried to explain that they arrived. Now, whether they came out of a vehicle or whether they had arrived on foot, I don't know, but they had their equipment with them and they reached that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone speak to those gentleman from the three of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to them as much as I could. I don't know their language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them sort of spoke some of my -- some words of my language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Mr. Petrovic seems to indicate that based on his recollection it was Momir Nikolic who was talking to them. Did you ever see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He also spoke to them. They stayed for about one or two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that's when at some point you gave those two gentleman a ride on the APC?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We offered to take them back to their unit and they wanted to ride with us towards Bratunac and Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at some point they asked you to turn around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, are you certain that they were Dutch? Could they have been English, say, United Nations military observers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I think those were -- well, be observers or -- I think they had their headquarters in Potocari. That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then you brought them back to Konjevic Polje. They got out. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then, according to Mr. Petrovic, Momir got into the armoured personnel carrier and all three of you returned to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I must say that a convey of buses came along carrying Muslims towards Milici and probably on towards Kladanj. The convoy was headed by the white jeep with the UN insignia with two persons, two soldiers, in it. They stopped when they saw the soldiers and those two soldiers then took off with them. And we remained there. They didn't stay in Konjevic Polje, nor did they return to Bratunac with us. They took off with those two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Right. And I apologise for not covering that detail. But my point is that the three of you, once they got out at some point, you, Mr. Petrovic, and Momir Nikolic drove back to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I could briefly show you what has been marked as D-37/1 for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry was the last question a reflection of what Mr. Petrovic was saying happened or what Mr. -- the objection is vague because that's not his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, see this is what we get into. I get and objection that I'm reading and now they object to what I'm characterising. But let me go back and I'll read back to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: My concern was not you reading or your paraphrasing. Were you having him confirm what Mr. Petrovic was saying, which is what you have been doing all along, or were you having him say this, because if that was the case, that's not what he testified to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's do it the easy way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's what I was trying to do, Your Honour. Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me read a portion of Mr. Petrovic's statement that he gave to the police. It's sort of in the middle of the page or it should be the second or third page. I'll just read it and tell me whether you recollect that. It states: "We drove for 2 kilometres toward Bratunac and the two Englishmen then said we should turn back, which we did. When we arrived in Konjevic Polje, the two Englishmen got out of the armoured personnel carrier. Momir said good-bye to them, and they got into their jeep and drove off towards Zvornik. Momir got into our armoured personnel carrier and we returned to Bratunac." Now, this is what Mr. Petrovic says. Is that your -- does your memory -- is your memory of the events the same with respect to what I just read?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Tell me what's different.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference is once we had returned there, they stayed with us for a while. It wasn't immediately that the convoy came along headed by the vehicle I talked about, the jeep. They stayed there for a while. And the convoy left for Milici, Kasaba Milici and further down. So they took a left turn and you take a right turn to go to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, aside from those details that are missing, is what Mr. Petrovic is saying here correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So he wasn't as thorough in his statement as you are here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but when they left, they didn't leave in the direction of Zvornik but rather in the opposite direction. They took a left turn back towards Milici Kasaba and further down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, let me show you what has been marked as D-37/1 for identification. And for the sake of efficiency, I will truncate my questions. On Sunday did you get a chance to look at this document when you were meeting with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the statement taken by the team investigator?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 29th of September, 2003. Is that the one you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's the one I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw this statement on Sunday. The Prosecution showed it to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you discuss it with him? Did you go over it line by line the way I'm doing here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you raise any objections at the time when you met the Prosecutor with respect to what's in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want to point out a couple of things in this document, though I had initially 12 items. Would it be fair to say that this statement is relatively consistent with a statement that Mr. Petrovic gave to the police approximately a month earlier? If you can recall from reading it, if you can't nema problema. Don't trouble yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to the relevance of that question. What relevance is his opinion whether or not this is consistent? I just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It will become consistent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think it's relevant, but the issue is, Mr. Karnavas, there is no need for you to produce these two more or less the same document to prove one thing, unless there is some new evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of 12 items, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no. I said I'm only going to cover a couple out of the 12. Initially I was going to go the old fashioned way and cover it all, but in light of the time limitations and the Court's rulings, I'm willing to truncate it to only a couple of points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Try to concentrate on those points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was, Your Honour, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just go and be direct. Mr. Petrovic in this statement indicates that when the two prisoners came into the APC, that Momir hit one on the head with a rifle butt. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that because behind my head or behind my back was the turret and the lid. So I didn't see what he did or whether he did anything. The door of the APC is at the back of the APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, he has also indicated that it would have been madness, in his opinion, to have even put six Muslim soldiers or six Muslims into the APC, given the size of it and the fact that Momir and Petrovic were armed. Do you have an opinion about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. What sort of an opinion am I supposed to have? The only thing I can say is that the APC was full of equipment. In addition to personal items belonging to members of UNPROFOR, bulletproof vests, that kind of thing, all the rest, they only took their personal items back to where they were billeted. They didn't take their bullet-proof vests with them, so there was equipment inside the APC. There were packages of water. I'm not sure if it was mineral water or the other water. I'm know that they didn't use water from our springs as drinking water because they were afraid it was poisoned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall ever seeing Mr. Petrovic throwing small cartons of water as you were driving down, down the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was giving out water from the APC from those packages that were inside the APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Finally Mr. Petrovic says that sometime in March or April, lawyers from Mr. Nikolic came to visit him and were asking him whether Mr. Blagojevic had personally given him orders to carry out tasks. And of course he said that he hadn't been given any orders by Mr. Blagojevic. My question to you is: Were you ever visited by these lawyers to see whether you could provide Mr. Nikolic with a statement that the orders that you had been receiving were from Colonel Blagojevic as opposed to or in addition to orders given by Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure when or what year, let alone what month, but I was visited by some lawyers. A lawyer from Bratunac was with them. I think he used to be a Judge earlier on. I didn't know whose lawyers they were and I wasn't interested. All they asked me was, "We heard that you had been to Banja Luka. Do you have anything to add to what you said there?" Meaning that probably there was something that I was supposed to tell them that I had failed to tell the Prosecutors. That's what they meant. I told them that I said everything in Banja Luka, that I had said everything in Banja Luka that I could remember. And I said, "I can repeat the whole story for you, if you like." I really don't know whose lawyers they were nor what their names were. However, recently, as I told the Prosecutor on Sunday, just before I came here, I received a summons to appear on the 22nd of October to give a statement related to the trial of Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic and Mr. Dragan Jokic. That's what the summons stated. I received a summons over the telephone. The man said what his name was, but I didn't get it. And the man said he was someone's lawyer. I believe he said he was from Bijeljina. He said, "I wish to speak to you. How long will you be in Bratunac for?" And I said, "I don't know. It depends on the Tribunal and how soon they will make it possible for me to travel. I may leave two or three days earlier and I have other things to do." But no one showed up. And he said, "Are you prepared to talk to me?" And I said, "I'm prepared to talk to anyone who approaches me. There is no problem, really." But no one showed up to talk to me about that. Then later Trivun Jovicic called and told me that the travel date was moved from the 25th to the 26th, and that's when I was supposed to appear before this Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Would it surprise you to learn that Mr. Petrovic in his statement says that you can confirm that he did not kill any prisoners as Nikolic has stated in his statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not surprised. I was present there while he went to the middle of the road and came back -- I mean, he went to the middle of the road. And would he kill men, five or six men, there in the road, in the middle of the crossroads? And two people were with us on the APC. I didn't hear him do that, see him do that. And I think he could not have done that. It was there in front of everyone. I was present. I was there. I was right by the APC. This was 10 metres away from me. I would have had to see this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it surprise you to learn that after Nikolic made a statement to the Prosecution, and even after he testified, the Prosecution never contacted Mr. Petrovic to give his account of the events?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, what is the relevance -- there is no relevance at all of what the Prosecution is doing regarding its investigation. This man -- this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I agree with you. Mr. Karnavas, do not involve the other party into your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Try to avoid any debate as much as possible between the two parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you did give a statement and the Prosecution did contact you. They were interested to hear what you had to say. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, you went to Banja Luka back on 28 November, 2001. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, there were several people there questioning you for a rather lengthy period of time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And by my counting, we have Bruce Bursik who was the investigator, there was Saleem Naqvi who was a lawyer, there was Sally Lattin who was an analyst and, of course, at some point even Peter McCloskey, the Prosecutor himself paid a visit toward the end to ask you some questions. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of the lines of questioning was about who was giving orders to the military police during those critical days.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And, of course, every time they would ask you, you would try to provide them with what you believe were true, accurate, and complete answers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I understand from what you've told us today that it wasn't until perhaps the time that you came to The Hague and visited the Prosecutor on Sunday that you had an opportunity to physically see transcribed what you had said back then in Banja Luka on tape. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive anything before, not in writing or recording of what I stated there in Banja Luka. Not from anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Because it says here on page 4 of the document itself, and it has been marked for identification purposes, for the record, as D-68/1. "That as soon as this transcription process is completed and as soon as possible, a day after, I'll make arrangements for you to get a copy of this manuscript in your own language." Why don't you look at page 5 and, for the record, the pages in your document -- just look at the last number because it's the -- the numbering system is rather different. So it would start with L0078302, is the first page. If you could go to page 5, which would be three pages later -- I mean, page 4 -- well, page 5 in your, and look at lines 14 to 15. The investigator for the Office of the Prosecution represented to you, "That as soon as this transcribing process is complete and as soon as possible, a day after, I'll make arrangements for you to get a copy of this transcript in your language." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I take it -- I take it you never got a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never had an opportunity to read it and to see whether you needed to make any corrections?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw this. I never received anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And, of course, since you never saw it and you didn't read it, when you came to prepare on Sunday, you were relying on your memory during that preparation process. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, might I ask, did the Prosecution give you the opportunity to first read your statement to perhaps refresh your recollection before they spoke with you or did they give you the statement afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never read this statement. I didn't read it on Sunday either. I never received this. The questioning in Banja Luka took 11 hours from 9.00 a.m. until 8.00 p.m., and I did not get this paper and I couldn't have read it that quickly, because there is so many pages here. I didn't read this on Sunday either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. But I'm skipping ahead a little bit to another area that we're going to discuss. But just while we're at it, yesterday you were asked a series of questions regarding a particular intercept when you were the deputy duty officer filling in for Momir Nikolic who had gone home. Do you recall those series of questions yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall those questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed that in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, my question: When you were meeting with the Prosecution on Sunday, did they extend the courtesy to you to review what you had said in Banja Luka and then give you the opportunity to comment on it to see whether your memory today, you know, was any different than back then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't. I don't know. They didn't show me this. I didn't remember what I said in Banja Luka, but I do remember some events that I remember well and I can talk about those things I remember well. And what I cannot remember, I cannot be certain of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Do you know whether they read to you in English with -- I take it there was a translator there on Sunday. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall whether they read from your transcript -- from the transcript of what you had said for you to hear what you had told them back in Banja Luka? If you recall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They read out to me this, this, which pertained to what I said -- what I said in relation to where the commander was, that I said that he was somewhere in the field. And it was differently formulated this sentence, the one I said then during that conversation, the intercept, as they call it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you, did they show you, did they physically show you a copy of the intercept written in your language for you to look at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is that -- did they also -- now, in addition to that, are you also saying they read to you what you had told them back in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't read it to me, but the gentleman, the Prosecutor said to me, "Do you remember what you said in Banja Luka? I'm asking you." And I said that I did remember what I said in Banja Luka and I remember what I said. So there was no need for him to read this out to me because I remembered what I had said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we're going to cover that topic later. All right. So right now if we could focus on another topic which is the orders. Because as I understand it from reading your transcript, there were a lot of questions put to you with respect to who was giving you orders. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, when you were in Banja Luka, do you recall being questioned about who was giving you direct orders, you as the -- in your position, who was giving you orders. Do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to go through your statement, just a snip here and there so we can see some of the answers that you gave them and give you an opportunity to see whether your recollection today is any different than it was back then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to that as not proper. For a statement like this, it could be used to impeach the witness or before impeachment to refresh his recollection, but that is after a question is asked. Now, Mr. Karnavas may ask a leading question based on information in that. For example, he can say: Did you not say such and such -- or was not such and such your commander? And the person says no, then he can refresh his recollection with this or he can impeach him depending on the situation. But for him -- it's not appropriate nor is it relevant for him to just go through this thing that was read at the time. This witness is here. He is before us. These same questions can be asked, and most of them were asked on direct and have been asked on cross. But to just rehash what is in his statement is not appropriate, is it time consuming and is not allowed in any courtroom I have ever been in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may respond very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I were back in the United States, I would concede the point to Mr. McCloskey, but we're not. And I'm sorry to say I'm not in the U.S. Federal Court. And I also take exception to some of the comments that he has made because there are areas that he has not covered on direct. I'm willing to adjust. Again, I'll go the middle way, but at some point I've got to do my cross in the best and most efficient way. And this is the way I see, given the rules we have established here in this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that the most efficient way is for you to put a question to this witness first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you did not get the answer you would, show this witness the document. I think that's the easiest way. If the witness totally agrees with you, there's no need for this document at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would generally agree with you, Your Honour. I would generally, but I will do it this way. I will do it this way, but forgive me if I'm not in total agreement, but I will do it this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It doesn't mean that I'm right and Your Honour is wrong. I'm just saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's no further comments about -- discussions between us. We have a witness here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall being asked who was giving you orders --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was being talked to at that time is not relevant at this point. This is a hearsay document. He can ask him a question who gave the orders, but at this time this is not relevant. There is nothing at question in this interview now. These rules have a reason and it is exactly the reason you stated. It's for simplicity, for clarity, and for credibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, we have already established that the question of order is a very important issue. There's no problem about it and the Prosecution asks the witness these questions and you, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall telling the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That is not relevant at this time what was said before. It may become relevant based on the answer to his questions. But the fundamental principle, he's got to ask questions before going into the hearsay and the records all the other material of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand your point, Mr. McCloskey. Just ask a direct question, because this issue, as I said, has already been settled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I mean the issue about asking the questions about the orders, it has already been settled. There's no question about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not a fact that you told the Prosecutor that you would receive orders from Nikolic or Commander Blagojevic, did you not state that in your statement to the Prosecutor I'm raising the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm raising the question because the Prosecutor made some insinuations, point to the person in this courtroom who also could give you the orders as if this gentleman never told him that he could take orders from Mr. Blagojevic. Trying to deliberately deceive the court that somehow he had never given orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Enough. I will not stand for any more allegations like this, Your Honour. It's absolutely uncalled for, and I apologise for losing my temper. But he has been accusing me constantly of vilifying Serbs which affects my ability in the area and my reputation. Now, for that kind of an unjustified comment, I will not stand for it and I apologise for raising my voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think both parties have to cool down on that issue. Why can't we for smooth proceedings, since the witness is in the courtroom. I think the behaviour of both parties will do a lot of damage to both of you. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We could have an early break today and we come back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm perfectly happy to go forward, Your Honour. I don't need a break, but if the Court wishes to have a break. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Then concentrate on your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have warned you, do not involve the other parties in this debate. (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those people would be Lieutenant Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was from the corps level, was he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also from Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was from the Main Staff, was he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also there were times when even General Mladic himself would order you. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You seem a little unsure. Do you recall telling the Prosecutor that Mr. Mladic -- General Mladic himself ordered you and Popovic to lead the convoy. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you told that to the investigator of the Office of the Prosecution, you were telling the truth, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that General Mladic ordered Popovic to start the transport, but I didn't know that there would be any escort. I didn't what the escort was for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But do you recall being asked who gave you the information in your answering, "Mladic personally ordered Popovic and myself." Do you recall stating that? It's on page 52 of the English version, lines 1 and 2. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this refers to exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If you could look in your version --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. We're going into the statement again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this is also on a matter where this witness has testified that he is confused, when Mladic and Popovic told him to do this, with one day for another. So this is misstating the testimony that's already occurred on this point and he's going back into this record without any impeachment and without any relevance for refreshing recollection. There's no question before the witness that he has a problem with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I think Mr. Karnavas asked a question and I think he saw the witness hesitated about his answer, he referred to this paragraph. I think in this instance, it's quite proper to do so. Mr. Karnavas, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look, sir -- actually, go back to page 51, lines 23 to 24. And in the English version it's the same basically. And I'm going to read along. You were asked: "Who gave you the instructions to escort these people from this elementary school out of Bratunac?" Page 51. You just have to look at the last two numbers on the pages at the top. You were asked by the investigator: "Who gave you the instruction to escort these people from this elementary school out of Bratunac?" Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you answer: "Not from the elementary school in Bratunac, but from the mechanical, the engineering school, from Bratunac." Then you go on, this is page 52, line 1: "Who gave you that instruction?" And your answer is: "Mladic personally ordered Popovic and myself." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall saying that, but I told the Prosecution clearly and I was clear when I said that yesterday during my testimony when examined by the Office of the Prosecutor. I confused these two days, our departure for Konjevic Polje and the escort for the convoy as far as the village near Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. This is what you stated, however, in Banja Luka. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we go to page 59, it will be 59 around lines 1 to 7 in your page. You also make another reference with respect to General Ratko Mladic. This would be -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now we're talking about a white transport vehicle, a white one in the United Nations according to the order of the commander General Mladic. And then you're asked: "And Popovic?" And you state: "In a Golf vehicle of the Army of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Are you saying that these are two different events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a Golf, dark blue, he was driving in front of me to the village near Zvornik. That's for sure! Was that Popovic driving it or somebody else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Popovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And -- but what I'm concerned is I want to make sure that I understand correctly. You're with the Bratunac Brigade. Are we to understand that General Mladic himself ordered you to perform a certain task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And of course if we look at the chain of command, according to what you stated earlier, you were supposed to be getting orders from your immediate komandir which was Momir Nikolic, and when he's not around, from Colonel Blagojevic himself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And yet according to your statement and your testimony, there were times when Popovic would directly order you or directly order your men to do certain tasks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because that's what the situation was like. The command of the Main Staff and the corps command were in Bratunac, both headquarters. And they had the authority to give orders to any member of the Bratunac Brigade, because the Bratunac Brigade is a unit subordinated to the corps and to the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was your understanding that if Mladic came and ordered you to do something, you had to do it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. That goes without saying. He was the commander of the Main Staff. He was the commander of the entire army. Of course he had to comply with his orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Beara? Why not tell Beara to go and ask Colonel Blagojevic whether he would permit you to carry out one of your tasks -- one of the tasks he was asking you to perform, if he did ask you any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Colonel Beara was most of the time staying at the staff headquarters. And he could have given orders even to commander Colonel Blagojevic by virtue of his position, the position that he was holding. He was a security officer with the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what about Popovic? Popovic is with the corps, the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Popovic was with the Drina Corps. He was superior to both the brigade and Nikolic. Of course, he too had the authority to issue orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in looking at your statement and listening to your testimony, it doesn't appear anywhere that you received during those critical days any orders from Colonel Blagojevic. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having received any orders whatsoever from the brigade commander, Colonel Blagojevic, at that time, not any, not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nor did you tell the Prosecution that you ever had received any orders from Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember ever saying that or receiving any such orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in fact, do you recall telling the Prosecutor that you don't even remember seeing Mr. Blagojevic during that period, that critical period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall saying that to the Office of the Prosecutor, and indeed I don't recall having seen him throughout that period. I may have seen him, but not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, you never saw him with General Mladic during that period, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you never saw him with General Krstic during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to talk to you a little bit about the intercept. As I understand it, on that particular night at approximately 3.30, you were asked to fill in for Momir Nikolic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when Momir Nikolic called you to take over his shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the same building where the military police were stationed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were outside -- you're at the front of the gate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The building where the military police were is outside the compound of the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And were you asleep or were you awake when Momir asked you to take over for him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that, whether I was asleep or awake. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it you can't remember whether you were looking outside your window to see who was coming in to go into the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't looking. I don't know. I wasn't looking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I take it you weren't the duty officer or you weren't -- yeah, you weren't the duty officer for the military police on that particular night, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So at some point, Momir Nikolic calls you and now you have to leave that building and go to the headquarters. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understand it, the duty officer's room is on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So as you would walk towards the building, there is an entrance. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's a long building. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With three different entrances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many entrances, but this is the first entrance on the right-hand side facing the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the one that you would have to go into?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, there are two separate rooms on the right side of the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two rooms. The duty room, the room where the duty officer was, led to another room, and that room in turn led to a third different room. That's how I remember it, but I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me show you what has been marked as D-70/1 for identification. And there are four separate pages. The first two are of the ground floor. The second two are of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
