utterances.text: Would you please lay some background for this map, who drew it, where you got it, is it accurate? Are we furnished with this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour -- well, for the record, I received them from Bratunac from -- my investigator received them from the factory there. And we were going to lay a foundation as to the exact layout of this through another witness. But as my understanding, in keeping with the rules, that subject to foundation or subject to connection, I could show the document to the gentleman and see whether he would accept or reject the document as it is, pointing out to him. If the Court doesn't wish for me to use the document, I could go along and continue with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, of course you can use this document, but at least you have to tell us the minimum foundations for you to use it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, let me ask you, the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade were in a factory, were they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a ceramic tiles factory for the manufacture of ceramic tiles prior to the war in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you ever been in that building and walked through it when it was the command post for the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had a restaurant in the same building. We had a restaurant there. That's where we ate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But also if you were the -- if you had to be the duty officer, you would at least have to go to that particular room. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as you walked through the building, first you -- the first room that you would go to would be the operations room. Would that be correct? If you recall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say the following: This entrance where the duty room was, as you enter the building, there's a corridor, which I can't seem to locate in this drawing. I'm not sure which way to turn it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, before we get to the drawing, sir -- before we get to the drawing --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to focus you verbally and then we'll get to the drawing. First you walk in --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the right entrance --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The right entrance, there was the toilet first. To the right was the door to a kind of conference room with a long table and chairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The room could hold quite a number of people. And then there was a table where the duty officer sat. There was a phone on the table. There was a TV set and there was another door there leading to another room --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which was the operations room --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- one or two rooms, and then from that room, that's where the duty officer was. And as for the other rooms, I didn't know, because I didn't use those rooms. It was only for the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would it be fair to say that from where you were, from the duty office room, you could not look out the window to see who was coming into the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't see the gate from that room. You don't see anyone entering the headquarters. The window is behind the duty officer, behind his back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And those windows look out on to the inside of the compound where there's no gate or entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you could not see anybody coming in or out of the headquarters once you got in to fill in the rest of the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, it's time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And by the way, as for the document D-70/1, the map of the headquarters, we found that there is some B/C/S subtitles. Could you please have it translated into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we might come back to this map tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, to prevent any further delay in the proceedings tomorrow, I would like to bring to the Trial Chamber's attention that the next witness, P-117 who I believe may be testifying on direct tomorrow, has custody of several notebooks that we have requested to review before his testimony. And it has become obvious to us or at least represented to us by the Prosecution that the witness did not bring these notebooks with him to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, thank you very much. I'm afraid that you have to come back tomorrow for this testimony and the usher will pull the blinds and show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. I am prepared to stay for as long as it takes, for as long as the Court requires me to. I have no problem with that. I'll stay for as long as necessary in order to be able to assist this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, I'm sorry to interrupt you. What is your request?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I'm sorry to be so hasty before the witness was away from the room. So please excuse me. I didn't want the Trial Chamber to rise and leave before I had a chance to bring this matter to the attention of the Court. We had requested to review original notebooks that had been in the custody of P-117 who will be testifying, I believe, tomorrow. These documents were referred to and provided in the Krstic trial as P-282 through basically P-294. The witness took them back with him to Republika Srpska or wherever he resides and made a promise to provide these documents when they were requested by the ICTY. It is my -- it was represented by the Prosecutor that this witness did not bring those notebooks with him, and if that's the case then we object to any line of testimony on any intercept, because this witness was the witness that the Prosecutor was relying upon to prove up the chain of custody of every document, every intercept, every bit of evidence related to intercepts in this case. And without these original documents to be reviewed by Mr. Stojanovic or our interpreter, we can't proceed with the questioning or even understand the direct of this witness. So we ask that either the witness be postponed until another time or the OTP provide us with those notebooks before we cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We even don't know whether those notebooks are relevant to the examination of this witness. Mr. McCloskey, can you shed us with some light?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Apparently this witness is a -- could we go into private session on this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
